title: Pant Pays the Price: Stripped of Vice-Captaincy and Axed from ODIs After Dismal IPL Campaign
excerpt: KL Rahul’s consistent IPL form earns him the Test deputy’s armband as selectors send a sharp message to the mercurial wicketkeeper-batsman
body:
Rishabh Pant has become the highest-profile casualty of India’s squad announcement for the upcoming Afghanistan series, losing his Test vice-captaincy to KL Rahul and being dropped from the one-day international squad altogether. The decision by the BCCI’s selection committee, led by chief selector Ajit Agarkar, marks the sharpest rebuke yet of a player whose talent has never been in question but whose form has fallen off a cliff.

## A Season to Forget

The numbers tell a brutal story. Pant managed just 251 runs from 12 innings in IPL 2026 while captaining Lucknow Super Giants to a last-place finish — tenth out of ten, eliminated well before the business end of the tournament. His strike rate dipped, his trademark audacity looked more reckless than inspired, and his leadership came under fire after a slow over-rate fine during LSG’s belated win over Chennai Super Kings.

For a player who was bought for a record ₹27 crore at the mega auction, this was a return that satisfied no one. The contrast with his replacement as vice-captain could not be starker.

## Rahul’s Quiet Ascendancy

KL Rahul, captaining Delhi Capitals to a respectable mid-table position, has compiled 533 runs this IPL season — fifth on the Orange Cap leaderboard. His consistency, composure under pressure, and tactical acumen with the gloves have made him the natural choice to deputise for Test captain Shubman Gill.

https://www.instagram.com/klrahul/

Agarkar was pointed in his explanation. “We want Rishabh to focus purely on his batting,” the chief selector said, carefully framing the demotion as an opportunity rather than a punishment. “He remains a vital part of our Test plans. But the vice-captaincy comes with responsibilities that can be a distraction when you’re trying to find your best form.”

## The Full Squad Picture

The Afghanistan series — a one-off Test followed by three ODIs, starting June 14 in Dharamshala — features several notable selection calls beyond Pant’s demotion. Jasprit Bumrah has been rested entirely as part of workload management ahead of a packed international calendar. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli return to the ODI setup, while Ishan Kishan earns a recall as wicketkeeper after an impressive IPL campaign with 490-plus runs for Mumbai Indians.

The Test squad introduces two uncapped faces — left-arm spinner Manav Suthar and Chandigarh’s pace-bowling all-rounder Gurnoor Brar — signalling selectors’ intent to expand the talent pool beyond the established core. Prince Yadav, LSG’s breakout fast bowler with 16 wickets this IPL, wins an ODI call-up despite his franchise’s struggles.

https://www.instagram.com/shubmangill/

## What This Means for Pant

It is worth noting what this decision is *not*: it is not the end of Pant’s international career. At 28, he remains one of the most destructive batsmen in world cricket when firing. His counter-attacking centuries in Sydney, Cape Town, and Birmingham are still fresh enough in selectors’ minds to guarantee him a Test spot.

But the message is unmistakable. Reputation alone no longer provides a safety net. Pant must now prove himself purely as a batsman in the Test against Afghanistan, shorn of the authority and status that the vice-captaincy conferred.

## The Diaspora Debate

For the millions of Indian cricket fans scattered across the United States, the United Kingdom, and Canada, the Pant saga will dominate WhatsApp groups and podcast discussions for weeks. He is perhaps the most polarising figure in Indian cricket — adored for his match-winning genius, criticised for his inconsistency and occasionally cavalier approach.

NRI fans who have snapped up tickets for India’s upcoming tours will be watching closely to see which version of Pant turns up. Those streaming the Afghanistan series from living rooms in Jersey City, Hounslow, and Brampton will be asking themselves the same question the selectors are: can the player who once counter-attacked his way to victory against Australia’s best bowling attack in the most hostile conditions find that gear again?

The answer will determine whether this is a temporary setback or the beginning of a longer reckoning for one of Indian cricket’s most compelling talents.
